To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) serializability of database concurrency control algorithms can be formally specified in temporal logic and formally verified using a classical logic theorem prover; (ii) the alternative specification method is more efficient than the traditional method; (iii) the verification system can be used to verify other concurrency control algorithms; and (iv) the verification system is a general-purpose tool that can be used to reason about concurrent systems in general.

1) serializability can be specified in a logic that is more expressive than linear temporal logic; 2) serializability of a concurrency control algorithm can be proven in a logic that uses classical reasoning; 3) the specification method for serializability is limited to the case where serializability is defined in terms of commutativity of operations; and 4) a serializability proof for multiversion-timestam algorithm is provided.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the specification of serializability and its verification in temporal logic.
the specification and proof of serializability in the temporal logic framework.
the specification and verification of concurrency control algorithms.
